messages:
sam: hitting a weird bundler + edge combo when using the TS SDK in our starter. webpack 5 build completes but Cloudflare worker fails at runtime with `ReferenceError: __dirname is not defined` and later `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'prototype')`.

sam: repo set to \"type: \"module\"\". import looks like `import { createClient, types } from '@redwood/inference'` and `import type { Client } from '@redwood/inference'` in a TS file.

violet: do you have any use of `import.meta.url` or `__dirname` polyfills anywhere? webworker targets don't provide Node builtins.

sam: no explicit __dirname usage in our code, but the bundled SDK runtime has a small helper that computes __dirname from `path.dirname(import.meta.url)`. webpack seems to rewrite it weirdly. bundle snippet from dist:```js
var __dirname = new URL('.', import.meta.url).pathname; // compiled helper
```

sam: in the built worker the helper resolves to an empty string and subsequent class definitions blow up with prototype errors.

harry: webpack config? target: 'webworker' or 'browserslist'? which devtool? some plugins transform import.meta.url incorrectly.

sam: webpack config uses `target: 'webworker'` and `experiments: { outputModule: true }` so we get ESM output. We're also using `ts-loader` in transpileOnly mode.

toni: I've seen two failure modes here: 1) bundler replaces import.meta.url with something non-portable, 2) bundler accidentally pulls the CJS runtime instead of the ESM build due to conditional exports and extension preference. Did you inspect node_modules/@redwood/inference to confirm which file webpack resolved?

sam: i inspected the resolved file in the webpack stats bundle and it points to an interop wrapper: `node_modules/@redwood/inference/dist/cjs/index.cjs` (surprising). That explains some of the runtime incompat.

violet: ok that tracks. webpack resolver probably prioritized the `require` conditional. Two immediate options: force resolution to ESM in webpack via `alias: { '@redwood/inference': path.resolve(__dirname, 'node_modules/@redwood/inference/dist/esm/index.mjs') }`, or add `resolve: { mainFields: ['browser', 'module', 'main'] }` so module entry is preferred.

sam: aliasing to ESM fixed the runtime in local testing. But TS still complains about `import type` losing types in IDEs because `types` are only under exports mapping and some TS setups don't follow conditional exports.

harry: SDK should ship a top-level `types` field and/or ensure `exports` includes an explicit \"types\" main mapping. Also consider publishing `module` field for bundlers that read it.

toni: for the sample app, short-term: add a tiny onboarding note in README and a webpack snippet to prefer module entry. Also include a minimal script to run `wrangler dev` or `miniflare` as smoke to catch this early.

sam: created a tiny repro branch and will open a sample-apps PR with the README + webpack patch. I'll also open an SDK issue linking the repro and the stack traces.

ops-bot: New issue: RED-PLAT/SDK#1750 created by sam  \"Webpack resolves CJS build; import.meta.url helper breaks in webworker/edge\"

harry: SDK follow-ups: 1) confirm `exports` resolution across webpack/vite/rollup, 2) consider adding `module` and top-level `types`, 3) include a tiny ESM-only entrypoint that avoids runtime helpers relying on Node builtins, 4) add bundler matrix CI (webpack, vite, rollup) that builds sample apps and runs miniflare smoke.

violet: also add tests for `import type` behavior in a narrow TS project so editors don't drop type hints for devs.

sam: PRs incoming. adding the webpack alias + README note now so new starters don't hit this on first run. will update with PR and SDK issue links.
